comparison: Perfect alignment on Ca2+-independent scrambling (C114-C116, C124-C127). Both identify the failure to capture closed-groove scrambling as a limitation. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to mixed results (TMEM16F agreement but nhTMEM16 discrepancy), while peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, noting the challenge of reconciling with experimental Ca2+-independent rates.

Strong alignment on simulation limitations (C129-C139). Both acknowledge rate discrepancies between simulation and experiment. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for the thorough analysis of limitations and appropriately cautious conclusions. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing the quantitative unreliability and recommending qualitative interpretation only. Both note elastic network and force field concerns.

High agreement on scrambling rates and open/closed differentiation (C35-C40, C44, C46, C48-C49, C51-C52). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative consistency with error estimates and experimental alignment (C102, C128). Peer reviewers confirm comprehensive capture of scrambling events and efficient differentiation between conformations.

Strong agreement on ion permeation findings (C82-C88, C103). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes consistency with experimental selectivity and appropriate caveats about low event counts. Peer reviewers acknowledge alignment with experimental findings on ion selectivity, treating this as supporting evidence rather than primary focus.

Agreement on membrane thinning observations (C54-C57, C104-C106). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative thresholds (14 Å thinning, 6 Å TM4-TM6 distance) and that thinning alone is insufficient. Peer reviewers accept the structural findings without challenge, noting substantial thinning in scrambling-competent structures.

Agreement on in-groove scrambling mechanism details (C68-C73, C76-C77). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes consistent mechanistic features with quantitative data (diffusion coefficients, energy barriers, Poisson distribution). Peer reviewers do not challenge these findings, acknowledging alignment with previous research on groove dynamics.

Agreement on concerns about out-of-groove scrambling (C90-C92, C117-C119, C123). Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the pathway is novel but speculative regarding physiological relevance, with unclear relationship to experimental basal activity. Peer reviewers express significant concerns about limited statistical robustness, lack of experimental validation, and speculative nature of alternative pathway claims.

Agreement on validation against experimental structures (C30-C32). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes qualitative agreement in membrane shapes and lipid densities with cryo-EM nanodiscs and AAMD simulations. Peer reviewers accept the qualitative comparison with Cryo-EM maps as a strength, with no challenges to experimental validation.

Agreement on groove-mediated scrambling mechanism (C53, C59, C107). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes groove dilation as the ultimate trigger with clear quantitative support. Peer reviewers accept the mechanism but note it primarily confirms previously reported findings, with no dispute about the mechanism itself.

Divergence on TMEM16K asymmetry (C41-C43). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, explaining asymmetry by structural differences providing mechanistic insight. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether elastic network restraints artificially create asymmetry and whether this is methodological artifact or genuine gatekeeping mechanism.

Agreement on experimental validation of scrambling competence (C102, C128). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes alignment with known experimental scrambling competence. Peer reviewers acknowledge the study captured hundreds of scrambling events and successfully differentiated between open and closed conformations.

Partial overlap on structure-specific variations (C62-C63). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for groove dynamics variations explaining rate differences. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN specifically for asymmetry concerns, questioning whether elastic network application creates artifacts affecting the scrambling mechanism.

Minimal overlap on groove mechanism (C5). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for comprehensive quantitative simulation results (C3-C6, C30-C34). Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for groove-mediated scrambling but emphasize it confirms prior findings rather than presenting novel insights.

Minimal overlap on simulation results (C4). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for internally consistent quantitative results across multiple figures. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for membrane thinning observations with no challenges to structural findings.

Minimal overlap on out-of-groove scrambling (C6). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for comprehensive simulation dataset. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN for out-of-groove pathway due to limited statistical robustness and lack of experimental validation.

Minimal overlap on simulation data (C3). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for quantitative results with robust statistical analysis. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for comprehensive scrambling event capture and open/closed differentiation.

Minimal overlap on structural validation (C122). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN for out-of-groove pathway speculation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for qualitative agreement with experimental structures, viewing validation positively.

OpenEval identifies that similar structural parameters yield different rates (C109-C113), requiring additional factors like membrane composition. Rated SUPPORTED with appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims about rate variations beyond primary determinants.

OpenEval discusses TMEM16A as non-scramblase with lipid insertion into vestibules and speculative hypothesis about membrane thinning facilitating ion permeation (C144-C153). Rated SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing TMEM16A ion channel mechanism.

OpenEval evaluates testing of prior hypothesis about specific residues (C74-C75), finding they contact many non-scrambling lipids, representing appropriate self-correction. Rated SUPPORTED as minor refinement. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific residue interaction claims.
